title: Rain Barrel Refill Opportunity
dataSources: Weather-station observations (`ecowitt:obs`, `weatherflow:obs`), air-quality readings (`purpleair:aqi`, `airgradient:sensor`), soil-moisture and greenhouse sensors (`plant:sensor`), aquarium controllers (`aquarium:sensor`).
app: Personal weather stations (Ecowitt/Ambient/Davis/WeatherFlow), air-quality sensors (PurpleAir/AirGradient), and aquarium/greenhouse/soil sensors via HEC and MQTT.

index=personal sourcetype=ecowitt:obs

description: Logs the days with enough rainfall to justify topping up rain barrels, moving seedlings outside, or skipping irrigation without second-guessing.
value: Not every garden decision needs machine learning; sometimes a clean rainfall threshold is enough to save water and hassle.
implementation: Forward local rainfall totals from your weather station; review rainy days and connect the metric to watering plans or barrel maintenance.
visualization: Daily bar chart of rainfall totals above the refill threshold.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Weather, Environment & Garden — typical feeds: Weather-station observations (`ecowitt:obs`, `weatherflow:obs`), air-quality readings (`purpleair:aqi`, `airgradient:sensor`), soil-moisture/greenhouse sensors, aquarium controllers (`aquarium:sensor`.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `ecowitt:obs`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=ecowitt:obs`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Personal weather stations (Ecowitt/Ambient/Davis/WeatherFlow), air-quality sensors (PurpleAir/AirGradient), and aquarium/greenhouse/soil sensors via HEC and MQTT..

**Author notes:** Forward local rainfall totals from your weather station; review rainy days and connect the metric to watering plans or barrel maintenance.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "ecowitt:obs", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=ecowitt:obs earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Rain Barrel Refill Opportunity** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=ecowitt:obs`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `rain_mm` (> 10) after sum — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `rain_mm`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=ecowitt:obs
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(rain_mm) as rain_mm by _time
| where rain_mm>10
| sort - _time
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=ecowitt:obs earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, rain_mm
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=ecowitt:obs earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `rain_mm` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=ecowitt:obs earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(rain_mm) AS p50 perc90(rain_mm) AS p90 perc99(rain_mm) AS p99 max(rain_mm) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.10.13: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Daily Bar Chart Of Rainfall Totals Above The Refill Threshold (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `ecowitt:obs` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=ecowitt:obs | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1d` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1d` buckets.
